title: Are You an Agile Learner
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article defines learning agility as the ability to adapt quickly and apply lessons from experience to unfamiliar situations, and outlines several ways to spot it in team members. Beyond obvious signs like challenging outdated approaches, it highlights subtler indicators: agile learners revise their opinions of people over time rather than locking in first impressions, and they can generate multiple alternative solutions to a problem rather than fixating on the first proposal. The piece identifies genuine excitement about new challenges as the strongest tell, distinguishing agile learners from peers who merely tolerate change.
points: Learning agility means adapting quickly and applying lessons to new, unfamiliar situations.
A subtle indicator: agile learners revise their impressions of people over time instead of anchoring on first impressions.
Another subtle sign is the ability to generate multiple alternative solutions rather than fixating on one.
Genuine excitement about new challenges, not just tolerance, is the strongest indicator.
quotes: The ability to learn quickly from experiences and apply that learning to new, unfamiliar situations suggests someone who has learning agility.
Unlike most people, who form a strong impression of others and then collect data to confirm that view, agile learners allow their opinions of others to change over time.
Agile learners aren't stuck or blinded by what has already been proposed to tackle an issue, but can easily generate other approaches or possibilities to expand the discussion.
Unlike most of their peers, agile learners are actually charged up by the prospect of change.
Given the importance of learning agility for organizations to thrive amid rapid and unpredictable change, you need to select and develop more team members who possess this crucial quality.
